## Epic complete — all four children closed, all four changes merged and Verified +1

| Story | Ticket | Gerrit | Merged commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 persist the record | `nonlineal-melancholy-grouper` (248f) | 1672 | `c638bc6947` |
| S2 confirm from snapshots | `soured-elmy-ostrich` (83d3) | 1683 | `3476af3d52` |
| S4 backfill at upgrade | `timeless-elusive-joey` (f6e9) | 1698 | `4a8e6a77ba` |
| S3 decline unconfirmed | `cinematic-untiring-dunnart` (47a0) | 1705 | `4010da6493` |

Every change carried `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` before submit; each was closed only after
its change merged.

## What the epic delivers

The blind spot: `managed_refs` marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY and is
strictly monotonic, so G3 proved OWNERSHIP, never that the peer had ever seen the link. G4 covered
that only when the outbound differ re-emitted the ADD, and `outbound_links._diff_links` dedups ADDs
direction-agnostically on `(vendor_type, target_key)` — "intentionally NOT deduped on relation" —
so a local `blocks` link colliding with an inward `Blocks` on the same pair was never pushed AND
never G4-protected. Post-e39f its removal record reached the applier and deleted a link the peer
never carried.

The fix follows the pattern both maintained comparisons converge on (GitHub ghas-jira-integration;
contrast softrams/bulwark): retain durable association/provenance and never treat an unqualified
missing link as deletion evidence. A removal is now honoured ONLY for a link some pass positively
proved the peer carries.

## The three acceptance criteria

- A removal record for a managed-but-never-peer-confirmed link is DECLINED and logged, and the
  decline count is surfaced in the per-pass INFO summary (this defect class was silent every time,
  so a silent fix would have repeated it).
- A removal for a peer-confirmed link still CONVERGES, relation-scoped exactly as e39f made it.
- Behavior is covered by behavioral tests through `_inbound_update_apply_links` /
  `compute_inbound_mutations`, never by asserting on logs.

## Design decisions worth carrying forward

- **Sidecar, not reducer state.** The record carries the vendor link id, while `_managed_refs` is
  deliberately provider-agnostic; a `.bridge_state` sidecar also survives ticket-log SNAPSHOT
  compaction structurally and emits no auto-pushed ticket event per link push.
- **Relation-scoped key** `(source_local_id, target_local_id, relation)`, matching the reader —
  NOT the direction-agnostic outbound dedup key, which cannot express that granularity.
- **Completeness is a trichotomy.** Absent `issuelinks` = unobserved, `[]` = authoritatively empty,
  populated = evidence. Consumed from `fetcher.merge_issuelinks_map` rather than reinvented.
  There is deliberately NO un-confirmation path: inferring deletion from absence is the very
  failure this epic removes.
- **One store instance** for the persist-phase evidence step. Two would defeat the same-pass
  provenance upgrade and, worse, race a LOST UPDATE where the later save discards the other's
  records. Pinned by a regression test.
- **Fail-open throughout.** An unopenable/corrupt store disables the decline and restores pre-a4bd
  behaviour; evidence is an optimisation of safety, never a precondition for applying a removal.

## Verification

- New suites: 20 (S1) + 14 (S2) + 13 (S4) + 10 (S3) tests.
- `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` -> 2551 passed at the final tree.
- Full CI-equivalent `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` -> 12504 passed / 60 skipped.
- Mutation checks recorded per story: the `_tracked_basenames` staging guard (S1), the
  no-downgrade skip and the true lost-update arrangement (S4), and the confirmation guard itself
  (S3, killed by four cells including the epic's motivating scenario).
- Five pre-existing cells in `test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` and `test_impossible_links_cicada.py`
  were given confirmation fixtures rather than workarounds — each models a peer that HELD a link and
  then deleted it, which by construction implies it was synchronized.
